canonical_policy.name: Modern standalone Angular
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code and organize application code primarily by feature.

reviews.boundary_analysis: New-code standalone/feature organization and integration/legacy exception covered; no speculative NgModule repair workaround.

context_quotes:
- Organize application code primarily by feature. Avoid application-wide technical buckets and empty architecture folders; keep feature-specific code within its feature and keep `core`/`shared` relatively small.
- Use route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component (default).

- Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code, organized by feature as `frontend-structure.md` requires; do not introduce NgModules for ordinary new feature work unless an integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires them (default).
- Use Signals for naturally synchronous, local UI state and RxJS when asynchronous streams, HTTP composition, cancellation, or event pipelines are clearer; avoid mechanical conversions between them (default).

Create directories only when they contain meaningful code. A feature owns its UI and frontend data-access; do not move feature code to `shared` just because two components of the same feature use it. `shared` suits reusable primitives that genuinely cross features (confirmation dialog, loading indicator, table primitive, formatting pipe).

Do not convert code to `any` to silence TypeScript, disable strict mode, suppress template diagnostics without understanding them, add NgModules to work around standalone configuration, replace framework APIs speculatively, or add another state-management or HTTP library to bypass a local issue (`.claude/rules/2-technology/angular.md`).

When Angular code is in scope, check `1-architecture/frontend-structure.md` and `2-technology/angular.md`: feature boundaries and component responsibility, HTTP calls behind data-access boundaries, subscription and reactive-state lifetime, frontend error handling, route guards not treated as authorization, unnecessary global/shared state, meaningful frontend tests. Do not apply backend project-boundary rules mechanically to Angular code.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Presentation/UI orchestration and meaningful explicit input/event conventions registered.

Route-level/page components coordinate UI behavior; reusable presentation components take explicit inputs and emit meaningful events.

canonical_policy.name: Frontend understands documented API errors
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Frontend code follows the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical and do not infer business behavior from arbitrary human-readable exception messages.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Contract/stable fields versus message text explicit; missing when-practical qualifier in skill already BF0058.
